lines.t: In the courts of consecration, where the blood runs down the side,
Where the fire never slumbers and the offering must die,
I can hear Your Spirit calling from the inner, holy place,
Past the veil of fear and memory into union face to face.
You, the once-for-all Atonement, went before with sprinkled blood,
Now You beckon living bodies to the altar in the flood.
Not with beasts without a blemish,
But with hearts laid bare and tried,
You invite us to the altar
Where the flame and love collide.
So I lay myself down on the blood-sprinkled altar,
Where the Forerunner opened the way.
First the Lamb upon the fire, then the ones who follow after,
Living offerings in His array.
Every wound, every sin, every secret in my members,
Every story burned into my frame,
On this altar of my body as a living sacrifice,
YahuShua, heal me in Your flame.
In the pattern of Leviticus, every part upon the pyre,
Head and heart and hidden sinews, all examined in the fire.
Childhood vows and old transgressions, thoughts and glances, touch and tongue,
All the stains in mind and body that have marked me since I’m young.
You, High Priest within the heavens, with Your own blood bearing in,
Bid me bring my whole existence, taking ownership of sin.
Not with coverings and fragments,
Not with half of what I am,
But in fullness on the altar,
For the love of God and Man.
So I lay myself down on the blood-sprinkled altar,
Where Your life was poured in love.
You went first beyond the curtain, as the Anchor and Forerunner,
Now Your healing flows from above.
Every wound, every sin, every memory I’ve hidden,
Every scar that shapes my stride,
As a living, burning offering on the altar of my body,
You make wholeness where I died.
This is priesthood in the Spirit,
Not the shadow, but the true—
At the altar of my person
You do what the fire can do.
You consume what must be ended,
You refine what You would keep,
Till the heart becomes a dwelling
For the Holy One who speaks.
Burn away the flesh that hinders,
Leave the fragrance You desire.
Burn away the bruised defiance,
Fill the temple with Your fire.
Burn away the early sorrows,
Seal the cracks from old abuse.
On this altar, YAHUWAH,
Let Your mercy be the noose.
So we lay ourselves down on the blood-sprinkled altar,
Where the pattern is complete—
Law and shadow in Leviticus,
Now fulfilled at Mercy’s seat.
Every wound, every sin, every story in our members,
We release into consuming flame—
We draw near to the One who dwells between the cherubim,
YahuShua YAHUWAH, all for Your Name.
From the altar through the curtain,
We arise in You, made certain.
